skill.name: browser-testing-with-screenshots
skill.description: Automates Chrome navigation, element selection, page inspection, JavaScript evaluation, and local screenshot capture through third-party browser tools.
skill.summary: Test web interfaces through Chrome with visual evidence and page-level inspection.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: Most external-command and upload alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples; screenshots remain local. Two dependency findings are confirmed because installation is unpinned. Semantic review identifies persistent session access, arbitrary page JavaScript, and potentially sensitive local artifacts.

remediation.issue: The required agent-tools dependency is cloned from a mutable branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed commit or release, verify its integrity, and document the exact supported version.

remediation.issue: Default startup can expose an existing Chrome profile and session cookies.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated profile and test account by default. Require explicit approval before preserving a profile or listing cookies.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and extracted content may retain confidential page data.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated output directory, redact sensitive values, restrict file permissions, and document cleanup expectations.

remediation.issue: Page-context JavaScript can read data and trigger state-changing actions.
remediation.suggestion: Limit evaluation to authorized test targets and require confirmation before destructive or production actions.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Browser Profile and Cookie Access
semantic_findings.description: Default browser startup preserves the user profile, and the skill can list cookies. Third-party browser tooling therefore receives access to authenticated sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly documents cookie listing and profile-preserving startup. Access is intentional, although no credential exfiltration is instructed.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Test Artifacts Stored Locally
semantic_findings.description: Screenshots and extracted page content are written to local files without redaction or cleanup guidance. Test artifacts can retain confidential application data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflows save page content and timestamped screenshots. The file provides no retention, redaction, or cleanup controls.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary JavaScript in Page Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports arbitrary JavaScript evaluation, including form-data extraction and synthetic clicks. Commands can alter application state or expose sensitive DOM data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly evaluate JavaScript for clicks, DOM queries, waits, and form-data extraction. This is intended capability with meaningful page-level privileges.

content.user_title: Test Web Interfaces with Chrome Screenshots
content.value_statement: Manual UI checks are slow and difficult to document. This skill guides Chrome navigation, interaction, inspection, and local screenshot capture for repeatable visual testing.
actual_capabilities: Starts Chrome with remote debugging through the required agent-tools package.
Navigates to specified pages and preserves or resets browser state.
Captures timestamped viewport screenshots as local files.
Selects page elements interactively and evaluates JavaScript in the page.
Extracts readable content, cookies, titles, and other page values.
limitations: Requires the separate agent-tools package and a compatible Chrome installation.
Uses shell commands and depends on browser scripts being available in PATH.
Provides workflow guidance rather than a maintained automated test suite.
Can expose authenticated sessions and sensitive page data when using a persistent profile.

use_cases.title: Verify Local UI Changes
use_cases.description: Navigate through a changed interface and capture evidence before and after each interaction.

use_cases.title: Document Manual Test Flows
use_cases.description: Repeat browser actions, inspect expected content, and retain screenshots for test records.

use_cases.title: Review Visual Behavior
use_cases.description: Check layouts and interactive states across important pages with consistent screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL] in a fresh Chrome profile, wait until [element] appears, capture a screenshot, and summarize the visible page state.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [workflow] on [URL]. Select elements interactively, capture screenshots before and after each action, and report visible failures.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an Authenticated Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [authenticated workflow] with an isolated test account. Check [expected elements], inspect page content, and save organized screenshot evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Visual Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [pages] for visual regressions. Capture consistent screenshots, evaluate [DOM assertions], document deviations, and avoid changing production data.

output_examples.input: Open the local login page, wait for the form, and capture a baseline screenshot.
output_examples.output: Chrome opened with a fresh profile. The login form became visible, and the baseline screenshot was saved locally.

output_examples.input: Test login with the dedicated test account and verify the dashboard navigation.
output: The login form accepted the test credentials.
The dashboard navigation appeared after submission.
Screenshots were saved before submission and after navigation.

output_examples.input: Check the profile and settings pages for missing content or visible layout problems.
output_examples.output: Both pages loaded and displayed their expected headings. The settings page showed one clipped control, documented in the saved screenshot.

best_practices: Use a fresh browser profile and dedicated test accounts unless preserved state is required.
Wait for specific page conditions before capturing evidence.
Review screenshots and extracted content for secrets before retaining or sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser tools against untrusted sites with a personal browser profile.
Do not use fixed sleep delays when a reliable page condition is available.
Do not interpolate unverified selectors or page data into JavaScript commands.

faq.question: Does this skill upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No. The documented command saves screenshots locally, but users should review the separate tool implementation before use.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: Chrome and the third-party agent-tools browser commands must be installed and available in PATH.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes. Use an isolated profile and dedicated test account to avoid exposing personal sessions.

faq.question: Can it test external websites?
faq.answer: Yes, but only test sites where you have authorization and avoid entering real secrets.

faq.question: Is it suitable for continuous integration?
faq.answer: It focuses on interactive Chrome workflows. Continuous integration may require additional display, browser, and tool configuration.

faq.question: Can it replace a test framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides guided browser checks and visual evidence, not assertions, fixtures, retries, or long-term test maintenance.
